page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 15.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The CPU architecture is x86_64, utilizing a 45 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 support. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests rank in the bottom 25%, indicating limited computational throughput. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also fall within the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression benchmarks register in the bottom 10%, reflecting constrained single-core execution speeds. Similarly, static web serving throughput and LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are positioned in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-standard-4 offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for entry-level general-purpose workloads. Given the lower benchmark scores, it represents a basic tier of compute resources where raw performance is traded off for standard resource allocation. This instance is best utilized for low-traffic web serving, basic development environments, light background processing, and small-scale database operations that do not require high IOPS or intensive CPU throughput.
